solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Settled lovers broken up by journalist

indicators.note: something broken up is split into pieces, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A couple's relationship ended because a reporter came between them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken up by' tempts an insertion, but 'broken up' is the anagram signal for LOVERS (giving RESOLV) and 'by' simply sets ED beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter that has been settled has been decided or sorted out for good.

clue.text: Leave about two

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a pair is two of something

explanation.surface: A couple on holiday, as in two on leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is to go there, so one must first leave where one is.

clue.text: Heavy table, say, marks when lifted

indicators.note: lifted means read upwards in this down clue, so the letters are turned round

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg
dots are small marks

explanation.surface: Raising a weighty table leaves marks on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'table' means fare, as in keeping a good table.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is filling, starchy food, a heavy kind of fare.

clue.text: Lazy morning, story with it

parts.note: a story can mean a fib
being in is being fashionable or with it

explanation.surface: A slow morning spent reading a trendy story.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-in is an extra stretch of sleep in bed in the morning.

clue.text: Yours truly rolling up to pub, try prohibition

indicators.note: rolling up means read upwards in this down clue, turning the word round

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
a bar is a pub
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: The writer turns up at a pub and tries to enforce a ban on drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, especially on trade.

clue.text: Book finished, throws a tantrum

parts.note: Acts of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament
when time is up, it is finished

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper on reaching the end of a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to behave badly, as a child does in a fit of temper.

clue.text: Prison officer from southern Ireland? One's taken to the bottle

indicators.note: from means the prison officer comes from the Irish place, so its name stands first

parts.note: Cork is a county and city in the south of Ireland
screw is slang for a prison warder

explanation.surface: An Irish prison guard who has turned to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken to the bottle' suggests a drinker; the tool is taken to a bottle to draw the cork.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is the tool one applies to a wine bottle to pull out its stopper.

clue.text: Securing wobbly table, firm strap

indicators.note: Securing means the firm word holds the rest inside it

parts.note: set means firm, as a jelly sets

indicators.note: wobbly suggests instability, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fixing an unsteady table with a strong strap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a business but means set, as a jelly sets; 'Securing' holds the 'wobbly' (rearranged) table letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat belt is the safety strap that holds a passenger in place.

clue.text: Singing hymns, my lad so drunk under piano

indicators.note: under means the rearranged letters come below the piano letter in this down clue

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tipsy young man sings hymns slumped beneath a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges MY LAD SO into SALMODY.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalmody is the singing of psalms and hymns in worship.

clue.text: Further note about dog breeder's first book

indicators.note: about means the postscript letters go around the other pieces

parts.note: a postscript, PS, is a note added further to a letter
Rover is the traditional name for a pet dog

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of breeder's is used

explanation.surface: An extra remark about a dog breeder's debut publication.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbs is a book of the Old Testament, a collection of wise sayings.

clue.text: Mistakes strike-breaker found in time

indicators.note: found in means the strike-breaker sits inside the period of time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is slang for a worker who breaks a strike, a scab

explanation.surface: Errors made by someone who crossed a picket line, discovered in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is the Latin plural for errors, used for a list of corrections in a printed book.

clue.text: Stop promotion

definitions.meaning: a mention giving publicity to a product

explanation.definitionFit: A plug stops a hole, and to plug a book is to give it publicity.

clue.text: Where army should have faith, as a rule?

definitions.meaning: soldiers should trust their commanding officer, putting faith in their general

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means usually, and read literally names where troops put their trust: in their general.

clue.text: Oil on skin, use sponge, wiping face

indicators.note: wiping face means the first letter of the whole string is wiped away

parts.note: to bum is to sponge or scrounge off others

explanation.surface: Advice on cleaning greasy skin: use a sponge on your face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wiping face' removes the front letter U from USEBUM; 'sponge' is the verb, not the bath item.
explanation.definitionFit: Sebum is the oily secretion of glands in the skin.

clue.text: Ebbing in Windsor, beautiful river

indicators.note: Ebbing says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tide going out in a lovely stretch of river at Windsor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ebbing' reverses ORBE, found across the end of Windsor and the start of beautiful.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebro is a major river of north-eastern Spain.

clue.text: Incarcerated supporter possibly, bit of a thinker

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment, one example of a supporter
someone locked up is in a cell

explanation.surface: A jailed football fan, perhaps, who is something of an intellectual.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain cell is a neuron, a tiny part of anyone who thinks.

clue.text: Hard to understand English from translation in Belgrade

indicators.note: a translation turns the letters of Belgrade into another form, here rearranged

explanation.surface: A text was confusing once English was translated into Serbian in Belgrade.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging BELGRADE gives the answer plus E, which 'from' takes away.
explanation.definitionFit: A garbled message is jumbled and so difficult to make sense of.

clue.text: Flannel perhaps, bang on mouth

parts.note: a clap is a sharp bang, as of thunder
trap is slang for mouth, as in shut your trap

explanation.surface: A washcloth hits someone right on the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flannel' is British for both a washcloth and evasive talk; the second is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is empty nonsense, of which flannel, smooth evasive talk, is a kind.

clue.text: Fibre approximately how old?

parts.note: a rough figure is an approximate one
asking how old is asking someone's age

explanation.surface: Someone guessing loosely at a person's age.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughage is dietary fibre, the indigestible part of plant food.

clue.text: Stretcher put on back of cart in terrible ordeal

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the rearranged letters
terrible suggests a mess, so these letters are rearranged
back of picks the final letter of cart

explanation.surface: A casualty laid on a stretcher at the rear of a cart after a dreadful experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretcher' suggests a medical litter; it is stretchy clothing. 'terrible' rearranges ORDEAL into LEOARD, with T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is a tight stretchy garment that a dancer pulls on.

clue.text: Dummy drugs

explanation.definitionFit: Dope means both a stupid person and drugs taken illicitly.

clue.text: Chicken perhaps yucky, it's said?

indicators.note: it's said means the word is heard spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: something yucky is foul, disgusting

explanation.surface: A diner suspects the chicken tastes disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicken is an example of a domestic bird kept for meat or eggs.

clue.text: Waste food?

definitions.meaning: to squander time or money bit by bit
a piece of food fried in batter

explanation.definitionFit: To fritter money away is to waste it, and a fritter is a battered fried morsel.

clue.text: Power cut's welcomed? Form a union

indicators.note: welcomed means the power letter is taken in

parts.note: a slice is a cut, and the 's stands for has
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A blackout is greeted gladly; people decide to join forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To splice is to join ropes or film, and to get spliced is to marry.

clue.text: Minimum of blasphemy, mild curse

indicators.note: Minimum of keeps the least possible part, the first letter

parts.note: light means mild, as a light breeze

explanation.surface: A gentle swear word with hardly any profanity.
explanation.definitionFit: A blight is a plague or affliction, something that brings ruin like a curse.

clue.text: Architect happy to knock back drink

indicators.note: knock back means the word for happy is turned round

parts.note: to be up is to be in high spirits
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A cheerful person happily downing a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock back' looks like drinking, but it reverses UP; Augustus Pugin was a Victorian Gothic Revival architect.
explanation.definitionFit: A.W.N. Pugin designed much of the Palace of Westminster's interior and Big Ben's tower.

clue.text: Cardinal rule for audition?

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word for rule is heard, not seen

parts.note: a principle is a rule or basic law

explanation.surface: Asks what governs a churchman's tryout.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means chief or most important, as in cardinal virtues.

clue.text: Initially clueless in recruiting candidates, ask around

indicators.note: Initially takes the opening letter of each of the next five words

explanation.surface: An inexperienced hiring manager asks other people for advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa is Latin for about, used before an approximate date.

clue.text: Blade puncturing sore, howled!

indicators.note: puncturing means the blade goes into the sore

parts.note: a sore, inflamed spot looks red
an oar has a blade, and blade can mean the oar itself

explanation.surface: Someone screamed when a knife pierced a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: To have roared is to have cried out loudly, much as when one howled.

clue.text: Best fish for bird

parts.note: the star of a team is its best player
ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: A recommendation on which fish to feed a pet bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common songbird with glossy speckled plumage.

clue.text: In control, be upbeat about foreign settlement

indicators.note: about means the letters found are turned round
In means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Advice to stay in charge yet cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' finds OLBEUP across control, be and upbeat; 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pueblo is a village or town in Spain, Latin America or the American Southwest.

clue.text: Famous person not losing heart with other ranks on deck

indicators.note: with puts the soldiers alongside, ahead of the rest

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
a big name is a celebrity

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of not is dropped

explanation.surface: A celebrity stays calm among ordinary sailors on a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like a ship's floor but is the verb to adorn.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a room is to decorate or adorn it, the verb sense of ornament.
